A year of product lunch and learns, in two days.

Two days with the latest products and applications across workplace, education, and healthcare design. Over 80 brands in full vignettes at Bakery Square, with the product experts behind them there to talk specifications, lead times, and how things hold up on a real project.

What Is MiniCon

Franklin's two-day product showcase, our local take on NeoCon.

You know the show. This year it is over 80 brands across furniture, flooring, interior construction, and specialty solutions, with the product experts from each manufacturer on the floor both days.

Free to attend, parking included. Each session below has its own registration link, and you can book a private session with AI expert Stacy Thorwart on either day.

Private sessions

AI expert Stacy Thorwart is coming to MiniCon.

Schedule a private session for your team, on either show day.

Stacy founded The Intelligent Designer in 2023, after a decade in commercial interiors and leading global AI strategy at the world’s largest office furniture manufacturer. She has trained more than 8,500 designers, and her courses are recognized by NCIDQ, ASID, and IDCEC. Franklin is hosting these sessions as a resource for the A+D firms we work alongside. No pitch and no product demo.

Designers trained8,500+ worldwide
Recognized byNCIDQ, ASID, and IDCEC
Format30 or 60 minutes, one firm
Stacy Thorwart Founder, The Intelligent Designer

Book a session

A personalized AI consultation for your firm

Pick 30 minutes or a full hour with Stacy, and your team sets the agenda. Most firms want the same four things: hours back on the tedious parts of a project, a straight read on which tools are worth the spend, a rollout the whole studio will follow, and proof it is working somewhere else first. She has worked through all of it with the design firms she trains.

Hours back on the tedious work

Where AI takes over the repetitive parts of a project, from documentation to spec research to the first pass at a schedule, and what that frees your team to spend the time on instead.

The tools she sees working

Which platforms are earning their keep at design firms right now, what they cost, and where each one fits in a studio workflow.

Rollout and governance

How to build an AI policy for HHSDR: what the firm allows, what stays away from client work, who owns it, and how to bring the whole studio along instead of a few early adopters.

What is working at other firms

The approaches paying off at the design firms Stacy trains, what made them stick, and the ones she would steer you away from.

Featured session

Helping K-12 districts turn priorities into a facilities plan.

Tuesday, November 3 at 3:30 pm, followed by our 2027 dog calendar unveiling happy hour.

Every K-12 project starts with priorities that are hard to put on paper. Engagement, belonging, school culture, a wider range of learners in buildings never designed with any of it in mind. Marisa walks through the workshops, activities, and discovery exercises that bring a district’s priorities into focus, how those insights become a roadmap for district-wide initiatives, and real district examples of what changed for students and educators.

WhenTuesday, Nov 3 at 3:30 pm
Where6501 Living Place, Bakery Square
Reserve a seat Happy hour starts at 4:30.
Marisa Sergnese Applied Research and Learning Consultant, Steelcase

Before Steelcase, Marisa was an experienced school administrator and adjunct faculty member. She holds a Master of Education and is an EDmarket Certified Learning Space Planner, and she built these exercises around the problems her own team was up against.
